# 30-second Workroom demo video for the homepage

## Context

The Workroom homepage needs a short, polished product demo video instead of (or alongside)
its current static hero screenshot. Joel has Screen Studio installed and wants to record the
footage himself, muted/looping, with on-screen captions (no voiceover) — matching the existing
hero image's caption-driven style.

**Corrected location:** the live homepage is **not** `~/dev/workroom/website/` (that's a static
draft copy). The deployed page is a Phlex view in the `codaset` Rails app:
`~/dev/codaset/app/views/pages/workroom.{rb,css,js}`, served at route `GET /workroom`. Its hero
renders a `<figure>` containing `img src="/images/workroom-app.png"` inside a `.product-broadcast`
panel (5px yellow top rail, dark `--ink` background, no macOS window chrome/shadow — the site's
"broadcast/teletext" design language deliberately avoids the soft centred-SaaS look). That same
image is the current annotated screenshot, and its callout labels ("Projects, workrooms &
branches", "Terminal splits · ⌘D", "Workroom splits", "Big, syntax-highlighted diffs",
"Changes · PRs · Notifications") are effectively a pre-approved shot list.

`~/dev/codaset` currently has **uncommitted WIP** on exactly the 3 files I'll be touching
(`workroom.rb`, `.css`, `.js` — an in-progress animated headline feature). My video-embed edit
must be additive and must not be staged or committed — leave it alongside Joel's WIP for him to
review and commit together. I also won't touch `~/dev/workroom/website/` (the draft copy) since
it isn't what's live; not worth keeping two copies in sync for this task.

`PRODUCT.md`/`.impeccable/homepage-brief.md` constraints that carry over to video captions: no
"beta" language, no invented metrics/customers/testimonials, and don't imply terminal sessions
persist across app restarts.

## Plan

### 1. Seed a demo fixture (scratch, outside any tracked repo)

Recreate the hero screenshot's demo project so the recording matches existing brand continuity
and doesn't expose real client code. In a fresh scratch directory (e.g. `~/dev/demo/acme-app`,
`git init`'d, not related to any of Joel's real projects):

- Two small workrooms via the `workroom` CLI: `session-login` (branch `feature/login`) and
  `rate-limiting` (branch `fix/rate-limit`) — same names as the existing screenshot/mechanism
  diagram, for visual continuity.
- Pre-bake each workroom with a ready-to-show, already-uncommitted diff (so nothing needs to be
  typed live on camera) — small, readable Ruby-ish files similar in spirit to the screenshot's
  `SessionsManager`/`authenticate!` diff.
- Give each a trivial `test`/`serve` script that prints fast, clean, believable output (green
  test pass summary; "ready" dev-server line) so terminal panes look real without slow installs.

This is throwaway and reversible; nothing here touches `workroom` or `codaset` git history.

### 2. Write the shooting script + Screen Studio settings, hand off to Joel

Deliver (not committed to any repo) a beat sheet for a 30-second silent loop, built from the
features already identified as most demo-worthy (`macapp/CLAUDE.md`, `RootView.swift` flow,
`NewWorkroomDialog`/`SetupOverlay`, `WorkroomSplitView`/`TerminalTabStrip`, `DiffViewer`,
`ToastStack`):

| 0:00–0:04 | Sidebar: `acme-app` expanded, two workrooms with live branch badges | "Every task gets its own room." |

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Run by workroom as a setup script. workroom executes us inside the new workroom
# directory and exposes WORKROOM_NAME, WORKROOM_PATH and WORKROOM_ROOT_PATH, so we
# take no arguments. See https://github.com/joelmoss/workroom#environment-variables.

# Returns 0 iff both paths exist and refer to the same underlying file (same
# device + inode). Catches the case where one path is a symlink to the other.
same_file() {
  local a="$1" b="$2"
  [[ -e "$a" && -e "$b" ]] || return 1

  local fmt='%d:%i'
  local sa sb
  if stat --version >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    sa=$(stat -Lc "$fmt" "$a")
    sb=$(stat -Lc "$fmt" "$b")
  else
    sa=$(stat -Lf "$fmt" "$a")
    sb=$(stat -Lf "$fmt" "$b")
  fi

  [[ "$sa" == "$sb" ]]
}

copy_claude_local_settings() {
  local src="${WORKROOM_ROOT_PATH}/.claude/settings.local.json"
  local dest="${WORKROOM_PATH}/.claude/settings.local.json"

  if [[ -f "$src" ]]; then
    cp "$src" "$dest"
    echo "Copied Claude local settings to workspace."
  fi
}

main() {
  local var
  for var in WORKROOM_NAME WORKROOM_PATH WORKROOM_ROOT_PATH; do
    if [[ -z "${!var:-}" ]]; then
      echo "ERROR: $var is not set. This script is meant to be run by workroom." >&2
      echo "See https://github.com/joelmoss/workroom#environment-variables." >&2
      exit 1
    fi
  done

  if same_file "$WORKROOM_ROOT_PATH" "$WORKROOM_PATH"; then
    echo "ERROR: WORKROOM_ROOT_PATH ('$WORKROOM_ROOT_PATH') resolves to the workspace directory. Aborting to avoid clobbering source files." >&2
    exit 1
  fi

  copy_claude_local_settings
}

main "$@"

# Run by workroom as a setup script. workroom executes us inside the new workroom
# directory and exposes WORKROOM_NAME, WORKROOM_PATH and WORKROOM_ROOT_PATH, so we
# take no arguments. See https://github.com/joelmoss/workroom#environment-variables.

# Returns 0 iff both paths exist and refer to the same underlying file (same
# device + inode). Catches the case where one path is a symlink to the other.
same_file() {
  local a="$1" b="$2"
  [[ -e "$a" && -e "$b" ]] || return 1

  local fmt='%d:%i'
  local sa sb
  if stat --version >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    sa=$(stat -Lc "$fmt" "$a")
    sb=$(stat -Lc "$fmt" "$b")
  else
    sa=$(stat -Lf "$fmt" "$a")
    sb=$(stat -Lf "$fmt" "$b")
  fi

  [[ "$sa" == "$sb" ]]
}

copy_claude_local_settings() {
  local src="${WORKROOM_ROOT_PATH}/.claude/settings.local.json"
  local dest="${WORKROOM_PATH}/.claude/settings.local.json"

  if [[ -f "$src" ]]; then
    cp "$src" "$dest"
    echo "Copied Claude local settings to workspace."
  fi
}

main() {
  local var
  for var in WORKROOM_NAME WORKROOM_PATH WORKROOM_ROOT_PATH; do
    if [[ -z "${!var:-}" ]]; then
      echo "ERROR: $var is not set. This script is meant to be run by workroom." >&2
      echo "See https://github.com/joelmoss/workroom#environment-variables." >&2
      exit 1
    fi
  done

  if same_file "$WORKROOM_ROOT_PATH" "$WORKROOM_PATH"; then
    echo "ERROR: WORKROOM_ROOT_PATH ('$WORKROOM_ROOT_PATH') resolves to the workspace directory. Aborting to avoid clobbering source files." >&2
    exit 1
  fi

  copy_claude_local_settings
